In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lack of external aid has been beneficial for Somaliland’s development of accountable political systems.
Somaliland is a good example of how a country can achieve a high level of peace and democracy without the help of external actors.
the Somaliland case demonstrates the possibility of peace-building without external assistance, and the potential benefits of this approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Somalilanders’ lack of access to foreign aid, and the consequent need to build the state from within, facilitated the development of a relatively accountable and effective government.

Somalilanders’ lack of foreign assistance and the absence of external actors in the statebuilding process allowed them to develop a political system that was more responsive to their needs than the political system in neighboring Somalia.

, in the absence of external assistance, Somalilanders have been able to build a state that is more accountable and more responsive to the needs of the population than many states that receive significant external assistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
external aid may have unintended consequences that undermine the very objectives it is intended to promote.
the international community should be more willing to support state-building efforts that are not directly tied to the delivery of external assistance.
external actors can facilitate peace building in fragile states by refraining from providing assistance.
